title: Local coordinates for a closed immersion of smooth schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be smooth morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion over $S$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every $y\in Y$ there are integers $a,b\geq0$, an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $i(y)$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and an etale $S$-morphism $h:U\to\mathbf A^{a+b}_S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space], such that $V=Y\times_XU$ is the scheme-theoretic inverse image of the coordinate subspace $\mathbf A^a_S\subseteq\mathbf A^{a+b}_S$ given by the last $b$ coordinates equal to zero, and $V\to\mathbf A^a_S$ is etale [def-pc-base-change]. The ideal sheaf of $V$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is generated by the pullbacks of those last $b$ coordinate functions, which form a regular sequence (each is a nonzerodivisor modulo its predecessors).

proof.text: Obtain affine regular equations for the smooth closed pair from [lem-pur-smooth-pair-regular-immersion]. Apply [lem-pur-smooth-closed-coordinate-lift] to get the prescribed coordinate square, etaleness on the closed subscheme, and ideal-generation and weak-regularity statements on every affine open.

Lift y to the pullback along the open inclusion. Apply [lem-pur-etale-near-regular-coordinate-fibre] to the already constructed map h and its coordinate fibre. It gives an open T in U on which h is etale. Take the image V of T in X and identify its scheme with T using the open-immersion image isomorphism.

Form the canonical map of pullbacks for V⊆U. Paste its pullback square with the original coordinate square; etale base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] proves the restricted v etale. For every affine W⊆V, its image W′⊆U is affine and the open immersion identifies their section rings. The kernel ideal pulls back by this ring isomorphism. Naturality identifies each last coordinate pullback with the image of its old pullback. Ideal spans commute with the ring isomorphism, and its additive equivalence transports each successive multiplication injection, hence weak regularity. These explicit transports finish every clause.

lean.statement: theorem Scheme.Hom.exists_etale_smooth_pair_coordinates {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ S) (q : Y ⟶ S) (i : Y ⟶ X) [Smooth p] [Smooth q] [IsClosedImmersion i] (hi : i ≫ p = q) (y : Y) : ∃ (a b : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) (_ : i y ∈ U) (h : U.toScheme ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (a + b))) S) (v : pullback i U.ι ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin a)) S), Etale h ∧ h ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (a + b))) S ↘ S) = U.ι ≫ p ∧ IsPullback v (pullback.snd i U.ι) (AffineSpace.zeroLastCoordinates S a b) h ∧ Etale v ∧ ∀ W : U.toScheme.affineOpens, (pullback.snd i U.ι).ker.ideal W = Ideal.span (Set.range (fun j : Fin b ↦ U.toScheme.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : W.1 ≤ ⊤)).op (h.appTop (AffineSpace.coord S (ULift.up (Fin.natAdd a j)))))) ∧ RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular Γ(U.toScheme, W) (List.ofFn (fun j : Fin b ↦ U.toScheme.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : W.1 ≤ ⊤)).op (h.appTop (AffineSpace.coord S (ULift.up (Fin.natAdd a j))))))
lean.note: The helper constructs the exact coordinate-subspace inclusion using AffineSpace.homOfVector, rather than assuming an arbitrary map. The ideal sheaf is specified on every affine open. IsWeaklyRegular there expresses successive nonzerodivisors, including opens disjoint from V; at points of V its final quotient is nonzero, giving the usual regular sequence.
